text: Normal pregnancy lasts 114 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days); knowing this helps plan for delivery. If delivery runs past 115 days, farrowing can be induced with a Prostaglandin injection to improve piglet survival chances — delivery starts a few hours after injection. Signs of approaching farrowing: 10 days before delivery the mammary glands enlarge and firm up and the vulva lips swell; 8–12 hours before delivery, milk appears when teats are pressed; 30–90 minutes before delivery, a blood-tinged oily fluid and meconium are passed. Farrowing itself: delivery starts 30–90 minutes after meconium is released and the first piglet appears. The piglet stays attached to the sow by the umbilical cord until it walks to the udder and the cord is cut. More piglets follow roughly every 15 minutes, up to 30 minutes apart in a normal delivery; total delivery time is usually under 2.5 hours, with the placenta delivered 2–4 hours after the last piglet.
